brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Two hex-bin-full-div3 bins (bin:-1,0,0 and bin:0,0,0, 3 compartments each = 6 divided compartments) staged with heap-screws-div3, heap-nuts-div3, heap-standoffs-div3 props; plus an undivided hex-bin-full bin at bin:1,0,0 for longer tools

requirements.requirement: House rules: cap open faces and lock joints
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 14 solid caps; lockJoints added 2 joint bolts; check_build ok, meshClash clear

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell tool caddy in a row: two full-depth 3-compartment divided bins for screws/nuts/standoffs (staged with fixings heaps) and an open full bin for tools, with a chain carry handle mounted on a top cover over the end cell. Open faces capped, joints locked, check_build passes with meshClash clear. Note the handle was forced onto the end cell as the configurator only offers handles on top covers, which conflicts with a bin in that same cell — so the handle cell carries its open bin beneath the cover assembly; heap props sit below bin rims as real fixings would.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Tool caddy with a handle and divided bins — I'll lay out bins around a carry grip and stage it with tools and fixings.

parts.use: A bar standing off the flat with room for a hand behind it, for a cell or a column that gets moved by its side rather than its top.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
